newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Dec 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Dec 13.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- South Africa's formerly white universities have been told by the government to expect multi-million rand subsidy cuts next year, throwing their budgets into disarray and raising the spectre of increased student protests as they are forced to trim student aid programmes. The money is expected to be reallocated to "historically black" universities.

- The recovery in the Premier Group Ltd continued in the six months to October with headline earnings rising 32 percent to 132.7 million rand after generally improved trading performances, with the exception of the fishing interest, chairman Doug Band said on Thrusday.
- The rand lost 8.5 cents against the U.S. dollar and nearly 10 cents on sterling in a sudden festive season sell-off on Thursday.
- South Africa's Mineworkers Investment Company is in talks with De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd with the intention of becoming the first black-owned enterprise to acquire a diamond sight.
- The troubled Premier Group on Thursday reported a 25 percent increase in headline earnings to 15.1 cents a share for the six months to October 31.
- The rand was trounced in thin trade on Thrusday marching to near to its all-time low bid on the dollar as stocks tumbled in record-breaking volumes.

- Marlin Corp Ltd, the granite produer, said on Thursday it would buy 56.2 percent of Kudu Granite Ltd from Germany's Deutsche Steinindustrie for 24 million rand, or 100 cents a share, with the help of Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd.
- The government locked horns with the country's wine industry on Thursday when Agriculture Minister Derek Hanekom moved to delay wine co-operative KWV's bid to become a private company.

- The African National Congress will present 60 amnesty applications, including those of three cabinet ministers and a deputy minister, to the "truth commission" on Friday -- a day ahead of the cut-off for applications.
- Safety and Security Secretary Azhar Cachalia has announced that 1.2 million rand will be spent on beefing up South Africa's criminal justice system over the next few years.
- The government is set to slap a ban on mercenary activities in the light of claims South Africans are involved in conflicts in other countries, including the Great Lakes region of Central Africa.
